spacr.figures.style.apply_axes_style.source:
Apply producer defaults once, before subsequent manual figure edits.

This is separate from finalization, which validates without restyling.
Image data, normalization, statistical results and numerical limits stay
unchanged. Explicit control identities are carried in the specification.
Stored manual choices apply after producer defaults and remain subject
to diagnostics rather than being silently reset.

:param ax: newly drawn Matplotlib axes.
:param spec: immutable resolved presentation specification.
:param layout: fit single-panel physical geometry when true.

spacr.figures.style.attach_colourbar.source:

Constant values receive a one-color key with one exact value label. The

single-panel and multi-panel owners.

:param ax: data axes owning the displayed scalar values.
:param mappable: original scalar image or point collection.
:param label: objective quantity represented by color.
:param unit: explicit declared measurement unit, or None.
:param constant_colour: explicit single colour for a collapsed scalar range;
    None retains the existing source map. Values and limits stay unchanged.
:returns: the independent Matplotlib colorbar, or None when no finite scalar values exist.

spacr.figures.style.finalize_figure.source:
Check declared semantics and rendered appearance without changing data or manual edits.

Unregistered figures receive an actionable diagnostic without an expensive
render. Geometry, opacity, references, fonts, contrast, error-bar ink and
rendered layout must all be checked before compliance can be reported.
Declared image and schematic panels are checked even with hidden axes.

:param figure: drawn Matplotlib figure to validate.
:param spec: panel specification, or None to use attached specifications.
:param diagnostics: render layout checks; false never certifies compliance.
:param record: attach the result to the figure; false supports read-only scene translation.
:param renderer: already drawn Matplotlib renderer; avoids another live-canvas draw.
:returns: immutable applicable-check and problem record attached to the figure.

spacr.figures.style.heatmap_image.source:
Draw unchanged heatmap values and mark each missing cell with a thin black cross.

The colour normalization is display-only. Its endpoints stay unchanged;
an explicit centre is used only when it lies strictly inside them.
Missing cells use a colour from the same scale and are distinguished by
the cross, rather than being presented as an extra numerical value.

:param ax: destination axes.
:param matrix: numerical matrix; masked or nonfinite cells remain missing.
:param cmap: colormap object or registered name, copied before changing its missing colour.
:param vmin: unchanged lower scale endpoint, or None for the existing finite minimum.
:param vmax: unchanged upper scale endpoint, or None for the existing finite maximum.
:param extent: optional image extent in plotted coordinates.
:param centre: explicit reference value, or None for ordinary normalization.
:param origin: unchanged image row origin, either upper or lower.
:param aspect: equal for categorical cells, or auto for continuous-coordinate density rasters.
:returns: the heatmap image; cross artists are added in place.

source_variants.arguments: ax, matrix, *, cmap, vmin, vmax, extent=None, centre=None, origin='upper', aspect='equal'

spacr.figures.style.pack_axes_geometry.source:
Pack declared panels with physical slot widths and aligned plot-area edges.

The requested width is a packing target. A categorical panel that needs
more room retains its physical slots and expands the page. All source
values, statistical calculations and numerical axis limits are retained.
Linked overlays contribute their actual text bounds to the primary panel
rather than being packed as a separate chart. Shared horizontal views
align their left edges across rows, and a visible shared vertical title
receives its own measured margin.

:param axes: ordered data axes with attached StyleSpec records.
:param maximum_width: preferred maximum page width in inches.
:param gap: spacing between neighboring panel envelopes in inches.
:param padding: outer page and measured-text padding in inches.
:param legend_space: reserve an external right column for figure legends.

spacr.figures.plates.score_ramp.before:
Create the diverging color map used for signed plate scores.

A hit score (SSMD, robust z, B-score) is signed about the negative
control, which is what a diverging map is for. The ends are the house

well scored below the control reads rust and one above it green, the
same as on a volcano.

:param target: ``"print"`` centres on a near-white; every other value on

:returns: A color map with a transparent bad-value color.

A condition with at most :data:`AUTO_N` values is a bar at its mean with

:returns: the kind drawn for each condition.
spacr.figures.style.condition_plot.source:
Draw one element per condition slot in the house style.

A condition with at most :data:`AUTO_N` values is a bar at its mean with
every value as a jittered point; one with more is a box (median,
quartiles, 5-95 % whiskers) or a violin with small points. At one thousand
observations the automatic form is a violin without individual points.
Single observations remain visible as points. Every element
is :data:`BAR_FRAC` of a slot wide and drawn at :data:`DATA_ALPHA`;
medians, whiskers and error lines are black at the same opacity;
the control is grey.

:param ax: the axes.
:param data: one sequence of values per condition.
:param colours: colours instead of the house series.
:param control: the control's index, or indexes.
:param kind: ``'auto'``, ``'bar'``, ``'box'`` or ``'violin'``, or captured
    per-condition forms for appearance-preserving replay.
:param many: what ``'auto'`` draws above :data:`AUTO_N` values.
:param points: overlay the values as jittered points.
:param seed: the jitter's random seed.
:param positions: x position of each condition; ``0 .. n-1`` by default.
:param labels: explicit source-group identities for portable recipes;
    display tick labels may be edited independently.
:param orientation: vertical or horizontal values, preserving channel binding.
:returns: the kind drawn for each condition.

spacr.figures.style.figure_problems.before:
What breaks the house rules in ``figure``, one sentence each.

Text under 8 pt, text cut off at the canvas edge, overlapping text,
error bars that are not black (or the screen theme's neutral ink, which
is the same rule on a dark page), and square-marked axes that are not
square. Tick labels outside the view limits are not drawn and are not
checked. An empty list means none were found.

:param figure: the matplotlib figure; it is drawn to measure the text.
:returns: one sentence per problem found.
spacr.figures.style.figure_problems.source:
What breaks the house rules in ``figure``, one sentence each.

Text under 8 pt, text cut off at the canvas edge, overlapping text,
error bars that are not black (or the screen theme's neutral ink, which
is the same rule on a dark page), and square-marked axes that are not
square. Tick labels outside the view limits are not drawn and are not
checked. Hidden axes and disabled axis decorations are excluded, while
visible image titles and overlay text remain checked. A temporary Agg
canvas is restored after measurement. An empty list means none were found.

:param figure: the Matplotlib figure to measure.
:param renderer: an already drawn renderer; None draws once for measurement.
:returns: one sentence per problem found.

spacr.plot.create_grouped_plot.before:
Plot grouped observations and run assumption-aware comparisons.

Pairwise tests are chosen independently by
:func:`spacr.figures.stats.compare`. Student's t, Welch's t, or
Mann-Whitney U is used according to the normality and equal-variance
checks; an underpowered assumption check selects the rank test. When at
least three groups jointly pass normality, Tukey HSD rows are added.

The ``'jitter_box'`` default is a statistical choice, not a
presentation preference: it shows the observations and their distribution
instead of reducing each group to a mean bar.
Two groups can have the same mean while having different spreads.
The box summarizes the distribution;
the jitter stays because the points are the evidence.

Parameters
----------
df : pandas.DataFrame
    Source observations.
grouping_column : str
    Categorical column defining groups.
data_column : str
    Numeric column to plot and compare.
graph_type : {'bar', 'violin', 'jitter', 'box', 'jitter_box'}, optional
    Plot representation. The default shows every observation together
    with median, quartiles, and whiskers.
summary_func : str or callable, optional
    Aggregation used by the bar representation.
order : sequence of str, optional
    Group order. By default, sort observed group values.
colors : palette-like, optional
    Colours passed to seaborn. By default, use the house data colour.
output_dir : path-like, optional
    Directory for saved output.
save : bool, optional
    Save the figure and ``test_results.csv`` when true.
y_lim : sequence of float, optional
    Two-element vertical-axis limits.
error_bar_type : {'std', 'sem'}, optional
    Error statistic for bar plots.

Returns
-------
figure : matplotlib.figure.Figure
    Displayed figure. It carries the source recipe used by the interactive
    representation menu.
results_df : pandas.DataFrame
    Normality, pairwise, and optional Tukey HSD results.

Raises
------
ValueError
    If a bar plot receives an unsupported ``error_bar_type``.

spacr.qt.preferences.auto_figure_colors.before:
What :data:`AUTO_FIGURE_COLOR` resolves to *right now*, as
``(background, text)``.

Public because a control that offers "Follow the theme" has to SHOW what
that currently means without storing it. Storing what this returns is the
bug the section header describes; previewing it is the fix.

TRANSPARENT, not the theme's window colour. "auto" used to resolve to
#000000 on a dark theme, which is where the black slab behind every plot
came from: an opaque black rectangle sitting on a container that is a
translucent SURFACE. ``bg`` is the window colour and a figure is not a
window (INVARIANTS 2).

Transparent also means the page-opacity preference reaches the plot for
free, and one value is right for both themes — baking in a grey would
freeze one opacity into every figure while everything around it kept
following the preference.

spacr.qt.widgets.fast_plots.EffectRankPl.before:
Every coefficient ranked by effect, as a dot with its interval.

The interactive twin of :func:`spacr.figures.panels.effect_rank`, and shows
what a volcano cannot: how large each effect is, and how certain. A volcano
ranks by significance, so an effect of 0.02 measured on six hundred wells
outranks one of 2.0 measured on four; ranking by the effect itself puts
them the other way round, and the interval drawn through each dot is what
says which of the two to believe.

Coefficients are drawn as dots and lines, not bars: a bar replaces every
observation with one height and hides the uncertainty of each estimate.

The saved panel draws the strongest fourteen and this one draws them all,
because a zoomable plot does not have to choose. The opening view is the
strongest :data:`LABELLED`, because that is as many names as a y-axis can
carry and still be read, and "Reset view" reaches the rest -- the same rule
:class:`GuideAgreementPlot` follows for its over-represented gene, and for
the same reason: a point outside the opening view is still a point, and a
point that was dropped is gone.

:param parent: parent widget.
Build the plot and its controls.

spacr.qt.widgets.fast_plots.EffectRankPl.before:
Draw ``frame`` ranked by absolute effect. Return the number of dots drawn.

:param frame: the coefficient table.
:param effect: the fitted-effect column.
:param error_column: the standard error, so an interval can be drawn.
    ``None`` looks for :data:`ERROR_COLUMNS`; a table carrying none
    gets dots and no bars, and the status line says the effects are
    drawn without their uncertainty rather than leaving a reader to
    assume they are exact.
:param significance_column: what decides the colour. ``None`` looks
    for :data:`CORRECTED_P_COLUMNS`; :data:`NO_SIGNIFICANCE` says this
    table has none, which is a different statement from "go and look".
:param label_column: the column a dot is named by when the frame
    carries no gene or guide of its own.
:param key_column: the identifier every other view joins on.
:param alpha: the cut a coefficient is coloured at.
:param drop_untested: leave the nuisance terms off, as the volcano and
    :func:`spacr.figures.panels.effect_rank` both do.

    The reason is not the axis. The volcano drops the intercept because
    it dominates the p-axis -- 3.6x the tallest real hit on plate1_dv.
    Measured on the TSG101 screen, its COEFFICIENT is 0.190 against a
    tested maximum of 4.37, so by effect it ranks 547 of 1,213 and
    stretches nothing at all.

    It is dropped because it is not a hypothesis. Its ``q_value`` is
    NaN -- ``perform_regression`` leaves the covariates out of the
    multiple-testing family -- so it would sit halfway down a ranked
    list of hypotheses, permanently grey, with no verdict available
    for it and nothing on the picture saying why. A fit carrying plate
    row and column terms has ~25 more of them.

Sorting changes the order: drawn dot n is the nth largest effect and
almost never row n of the table. The frame rows are therefore carried
through the sort explicitly (``rows=``) rather than re-derived from the
drawing order -- see :meth:`FastPlot.add_scatter`, where the same trap
is written out for the Q-Q.

spacr.qt.widgets.graph_builder.before:
Graph Builder — drag a column onto a channel and the chart appears.

A drag-and-drop alternative to choosing among the forty ``plot_*`` functions
and their arguments. Six drop zones — x, y, colour, size, facet-row,
facet-column — a well of the columns worth plotting, and a canvas that
re-renders the moment a zone changes.

What is in here and what is not
-------------------------------

Everything about *what to draw* lives in :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec`:
the spec object, the plot-type inference, the facet grid, the shared scales and
the large-data policy. This module is the chrome and the matplotlib calls. The
split exists because small multiples, the gate editor, the feature explorer and
the campaign control charts are all "the graph builder with one more rule", and
they need the engine without inheriting a drag-and-drop panel.

Linked, and asymmetric on purpose
---------------------------------

:class:`GraphCanvas` mixes in
:class:`spacr.qt.linked_selection.LinkedView`, so it is one of the views that
talk to each other:

* a **brush** (drag a rectangle across a panel) publishes the rows it swept as
  the shared selection;
* an incoming **selection** rings those rows and dims the rest. It never
  removes a point — a selection highlights, it does not hide;
* an incoming **filter** does remove rows, and the axes re-scale to what is
  left, because a filter genuinely narrows the population.

The brush is evaluated as a *predicate over the frame*, not as a hit test
against drawn marks, which is what keeps it exact when a panel was drawn as a
density raster or from a sample.

Colour
------

Categorical series take a fixed eight-hue order — never cycled, never
re-assigned when a filter changes the series count, so a gene keeps its colour
between two charts. The order is the validated reference palette (light and
dark steps kept separately rather than flipped), and a continuous colour column
gets a single-hue light-to-dark ramp. Beyond eight levels the extras fold into
one "other" grey rather than adding hues that are hard to tell apart.

spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_view.before:
The trellis surface — the Graph Builder's canvas, laid out as a grid.

:class:`TrellisCanvas` **subclasses**
:class:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_builder.GraphCanvas` rather than reimplementing
it. The mark drawing, the fixed
categorical hue order, the density raster, the selection ring, the legend and
the brush are one implementation, and a second one would be a second set of
rules to keep in step with the first — the mistake
:mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.pivot_builder` avoids by not drawing anything at all.

What the subclass changes is the two things a trellis is:

* **the layout** comes from :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_spec.trellis`,
  which knows about wrapping and about blank slots, rather than from
  ``facet_grid`` directly;
* **the scales are set per panel from that panel's own group**. Every panel's
  limits are written explicitly rather than left to matplotlib's ``sharex``:
  sharing makes panels agree with *each other*, but on whatever the first one
  autoscaled to, which is not necessarily wide enough for the rest. Under
  :data:`~spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_spec.SCALE_SHARED` — the default — every
  panel is handed the identical tuple, which is a property a test can assert
  and an eye can trust.

Two conventions of the grid
---------------------------

**Inner tick labels are hidden only when the axis is genuinely shared.** A
trellis with per-panel scales that hid its inner ticks would misstate the
scales; if a panel has its own limits it prints its own numbers.

**Every panel's title carries its n**, from
:meth:`~spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_spec.TrellisPanel.label`. Blank slots at the
end of a wrapped grid are hidden entirely — they are not panels with no data,
they are the remainder of a division.

Plot grouped observations and run assumption-aware comparisons.

Pairwise tests are chosen independently by
:func:`spacr.figures.stats.compare`. Student's t, Welch's t, or
Mann-Whitney U is used according to the normality and equal-variance
checks; an underpowered assumption check selects the rank test. When at
least three groups jointly pass normality, Tukey HSD rows are added.

The ``'jitter_box'`` default is a statistical choice, not a
presentation preference: it shows the observations and their distribution
instead of reducing each group to a mean bar.
Two groups can have the same mean while having different spreads.
The box summarizes the distribution;
the jitter stays because the points are the evidence.

----------

    Source observations.

    Categorical column defining groups.
data_column : str
    Numeric column to plot and compare.
graph_type : {'bar', 'violin', 'jitter', 'box', 'jitter_box'}, optional
    Plot representation. The default shows every observation together
    with median, quartiles, and whiskers.
summary_func : str or callable, optional
    Aggregation used by the bar representation.
order : sequence of str, optional
    Group order. By default, sort observed group values.
colors : palette-like, optional

    representation menu.

least three groups jointly pass normality, Tukey HSD rows are added.

twenty values, a box with observations above twenty, and a violin without

available. Statistical comparisons and exported results do not depend on

and ``experimental_unit`` declare scientific context for the legend.

before.docstring:
Every coefficient ranked by effect, as a dot with its interval.

The interactive twin of :func:`spacr.figures.panels.effect_rank`, and shows
what a volcano cannot: how large each effect is, and how certain. A volcano
ranks by significance, so an effect of 0.02 measured on six hundred wells
outranks one of 2.0 measured on four; ranking by the effect itself puts
them the other way round, and the interval drawn through each dot is what
says which of the two to believe.

Coefficients are drawn as dots and lines, not bars: a bar replaces every
observation with one height and hides the uncertainty of each estimate.

The saved panel draws the strongest fourteen and this one draws them all,
because a zoomable plot does not have to choose. The opening view is the
strongest :data:`LABELLED`, because that is as many names as a y-axis can
carry and still be read, and "Reset view" reaches the rest -- the same rule
:class:`GuideAgreementPlot` follows for its over-represented gene, and for
the same reason: a point outside the opening view is still a point, and a
point that was dropped is gone.

:param parent: parent widget.
Build the plot and its controls.

    ``None`` looks for :data:`ERROR_COLUMNS`; a table carrying none
    gets dots and no bars, and the status line says the effects are
    drawn without their uncertainty rather than leaving a reader to
    assume they are exact.
:param significance_column: what decides the colour. ``None`` looks
    for :data:`CORRECTED_P_COLUMNS`; :data:`NO_SIGNIFICANCE` says this
    table has none, which is a different statement from "go and look".

    carries no gene or guide of its own.

:param alpha: the cut a coefficient is coloured at.
:param drop_untested: leave the nuisance terms off, as the volcano and
    :func:`spacr.figures.panels.effect_rank` both do.

    The reason is not the axis. The volcano drops the intercept because
    it dominates the p-axis -- 3.6x the tallest real hit on plate1_dv.
    Measured on the TSG101 screen, its COEFFICIENT is 0.190 against a
    tested maximum of 4.37, so by effect it ranks 547 of 1,213 and
    stretches nothing at all.

    It is dropped because it is not a hypothesis. Its ``q_value`` is
    NaN -- ``perform_regression`` leaves the covariates out of the
    multiple-testing family -- so it would sit halfway down a ranked
    list of hypotheses, permanently grey, with no verdict available
    for it and nothing on the picture saying why. A fit carrying plate
    row and column terms has ~25 more of them.

almost never row n of the table. The frame rows are therefore carried
through the sort explicitly (``rows=``) rather than re-derived from the
drawing order -- see :meth:`FastPlot.add_scatter`, where the same trap
is written out for the Q-Q.
